_readme: SS-306. og:title / og:description are allowed to differ from the page title and
description ONLY where the divergence is declared here. Undeclared divergence is an
error, because drift and deliberate social copy look identical in a diff.
Seeded 2026-08-20 with the 9 title and 11 description divergences that already
existed, all marked TODO(pappy). REVIEWED 2026-08-26: six were drift and were
resolved by aligning the page and og values and deleting the entry -- one on / as
part of the homepage retitle, then /etl-showcase (title and description),
remain are real patterns and each reason now says which one, so the next reader can
disagree with a specific decision rather than with a placeholder.
THE TWO PATTERNS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ADDING ONE:
- og:title drops the "| SiegeStack" suffix. A card already shows the domain.
- og:description may exceed the 120-160 SS-302 allows for a meta description,
and several deliberately do. Shortening FOR social is the giveaway of drift,
not intent -- og is the surface with more room, not less.
SS-306 DOES NOT POLICE twitter:title OR twitter:description AT ALL. Half of every
divergence on this site was therefore never reported. Where an og value was
aligned above, its twitter twin was brought with it by hand.

overrides.reason: Intentional, and this one is a reorder rather than a trim. The page title leads with the person because that is what someone searching for it typed. A shared card leads with the brand because the reader has usually not heard of either yet.

overrides.pageValue: Why Your ERP Report Times Out on Month-to-Date | SiegeStack
overrides.ogValue: Why Your ERP Report Times Out on Month-to-Date
overrides.reason: Intentional: og:title is the page title without the "| SiegeStack" suffix. A social card already shows the domain, so the suffix is duplicated chrome in the one place the brand is never ambiguous. Same pattern on /prophet-21 and /sql-server-erp-performance.

overrides.pageValue: A report that is instant for today and times out for month-to-date is rarely a volume problem. How to diagnose the missing index and apply it safely.
overrides.ogValue: Fast on today, dead on month-to-date. It is an access-path problem, not a volume problem — and the fix is usually one index.
overrides.reason: Intentional: a hook rather than a summary. "Fast on today, dead on month-to-date" is the symptom in the reader's own words; the meta description has to be the version that reads well under a blue link.

Intentional: the page title states the thesis in the colon clause ("Consolidate First") and the og title states it as the full phrase, "Consolidate, Then Optimize", because a card has room for the whole idea and a SERP line does not.

overrides.pageValue: Running two systems of record? Consolidate onto one, then optimize slotting, order consolidation, purchasing and network replenishment on top of it.
overrides.ogValue: Two systems of record make every network-level answer wrong in ways nobody can see. Consolidate first, then optimize. A staged engagement model.
overrides.reason: Intentional: the og copy names the consequence ("every network-level answer wrong in ways nobody can see") that the 160-character meta description has no room for.

overrides.pageValue: What a Prophet 21 Upgrade Does to Reporting | SiegeStack
overrides.ogValue: What a Prophet 21 Upgrade Does to Your Reporting
overrides.reason: Intentional: suffix dropped, and "Your" restored. The page title has to lose it to stay inside SS-301's 60 characters; og:title has no such cap, so the sentence reads the way it was written.

overrides.pageValue: Three different things get called a P21 upgrade. What each does to custom reports, indexes and integrations on Epicor Prophet 21, and the baseline to capture.
overrides.ogValue: A version upgrade, the desktop-to-web move, and replacing P21 with Kinetic are three different projects. What each one does to reporting built on a vendor schema.
overrides.reason: Intentional: 163 characters, deliberately over what SS-302 allows a meta description. og has no such limit, and the extra room is spent naming all three things people call an upgrade.

overrides.ogValue: Epicor P21 & Kinetic Reporting and Integration
overrides.reason: Intentional: page title minus the "| SiegeStack" suffix, for the same reason as /erp-report-slow-month-to-date. No other difference.

overrides.pageValue: Reporting and integration on Epicor Prophet 21 and Kinetic: the data-model traps that make P21 reports quietly wrong, and what a vendor schema changes.
overrides.ogValue: The P21 data-model traps that make reports quietly wrong — open versus posted, undated lines, unmapped identity — and what changes when the schema is the vendor
overrides.reason: Intentional: the og copy enumerates the traps -- open versus posted, undated lines, unmapped identity -- where the meta description can only say that traps exist. NOTE: this value was truncated at an apostrophe in data/pages.json until 2026-08-26; the page was always correct.

overrides.pageValue: SQL Server Performance for ERP Reporting | SiegeStack
overrides.ogValue: SQL Server Performance for ERP Reporting

overrides.ogValue: How to Use Claude AI Effectively: A Real Workflow That Ships Production Work

overrides.reason: Intentional: opens on the objection ("Stop treating Claude like a chatbot") instead of the topic, and names Claude vs ChatGPT, which is a query people actually type. NOTE: this value was truncated at an apostrophe in data/pages.json until 2026-08-26; the page was always correct.
